parole.significato: Genista tridentata, a plant native to the Iberian peninsula
parole.testo: From substrate *carcasia, *querquesia, or similar, from Celtic, from Proto-Indo-European *pérkus ~ *pr̥kʷéu- (“oak”). Compare the local pre-Roman tribal name Querquerni abd Galician carqueixa.

parole.significato: top of a conical structure, heap or mountain
parole.testo: Attested since the 12th century, in Latin charters. Probably from a substrate language; compare Proto-Celtic *kruttos (“round object”): Welsh crwth (“hump, hunch”). Compare Galician cruto and Asturian corollu.

parole.significato: trunk and roots of heather, traditionally used in the production of coal

parole.significato: ankle (each of the bony protrusions (external and internal) that are found in the region of the joint between the leg a…
parole.testo: From Middle Portuguese tormezelo, from Old Galician-Portuguese, from *turmo (“bulk, swelling”) + -celo, from a substrate language. Cognate with Galician tornecelo and probably with Catalan turmell and Occitan turmel.
